title: The Idea of Thin Places
core_idea: Some traditions speak of thin places where the unseen feels close; whatever one believes, such moments can invite deeper presence.
text: Some old traditions speak of thin places. A shoreline at dusk. A hilltop in the mist. A quiet room where someone was deeply loved. In these places, people say, the distance between this world and something beyond it seems to grow small. No one can prove that, and you don't need to. Many of us have felt a moment like it anyway, a sudden stillness, a sense of being held by something larger. Perhaps a thin place is less about location and more about attention. When you slow down enough, ordinary ground can feel quietly sacred.
description: A reflection on the old idea of thin places, and how slowing down can make ordinary moments feel sacred.
